segments.text: Alertmanager tells you that something is wrong. Jarvis helps your team do something about it.
Jarvis connects all your Alertmanager clusters, from development to production, in one view.
Every change is pushed live to your browser. When a new alert fires, it simply appears. No refresh needed.
Search across every alert. Type a few letters, and only what matters stays on screen.
Save the filters you need every day, and switch between them with a single click.
Open any alert to see its labels, its links, and a heatmap of when it fired. The full history is stored, so nothing gets lost after a restart.
Claim an alert with one click, so everyone knows who is on it. Add a short note, and it shows up right on the card for the whole team.
Comments stay with the alert, even when it fires again, so the next person on call knows the whole story.
Silencing is at the heart of Jarvis. Fast-Silence mutes an alert in one click, for as long as you choose.
For more control, open the full silence form. Before you create it, Jarvis shows exactly which alerts will be affected.
A whole group of alerts can be silenced at once, with the same preview.
Recurring maintenance windows become reusable templates. Pick one, and the matchers and reason are filled in for you.
And every silence is managed on its own page, where you can extend, edit or expire it.
Secure Jarvis the way you need it: open for trusted networks, with built-in user management, or with single sign-on through any OIDC provider.
It runs as a single container. Start with SQLite, move to PostgreSQL, and scale to a highly available setup on Kubernetes with the Helm chart.
Every release ships signed container images and a software bill of materials, and the container runs hardened by default.
Jarvis is free and open source. Get started on GitHub, at k j one eight seven slash jarvis.
